chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar said: al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban narrated from Muhammad ibn Auramah, from Ibn Mahbub, from Salih ibn Hamzah, from Aban, from Asad, from al-Mufaddal ibn Umar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Whoever claims that Allah is in a thing, from a thing, or on a thing, has become an infidel. If Allah, the Mighty and High, were on something then He would have been carried. If He were in something then He would have been surrounded, and if He were from something then He would have been caused.

key_terms.أَشْرَكَ: To associate partners with God; to commit shirk
key_terms.مَحْمُولًا: Carried or borne (implying being placed upon a support)
key_terms.مُحْدَثًا: Created, caused, or originated (implying having a beginning)

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Sadiq explain the concept of Allah's transcendence beyond space and direction?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) elucidates the doctrine of *Tanzih* (divine transcendence) by negating spatial dimensions (*jism*) and directionality to preserve Allah's absolute independence from creation. It employs logical deduction to show that if God were 'on' a thing, He would be subject to gravity and motion; if 'in' a thing, He would be confined and limited; and if 'from' a thing, He would be contingent and created, thereby falling into *shirk*. This reasoning is foundational in Shia kalām for refuting anthropomorphic views and affirming that God is not a body (*jism*) nor located in space or time.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 9. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (RA) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-`Attar said: al-Husayn ibn al-Hasan ibn Aban said, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Auramah, on the authority of Ibn Mahbub, on the authority of Salih ibn Hamzah, on the authority of Aban, on the authority of Asad, on the authority of al-Mufaddal ibn `Umar that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS) said:

Whoever claims that Allah is in a thing, from a thing, or on a thing, has become an infidel. If Allah, the Mighty and High, were on something then He would have been carried. If He were in something then He would have been surrounded, and if He were from something then He would have been caused.
